import pandas as pd
import numpy as np


def _norm_sku(s):
    if pd.isna(s):
        return np.nan
    return str(s).strip().upper()


def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    orders = inputs["orders"].copy()
    price_list = inputs["price_list"].copy()

    # ---- expression: sku_norm = UPPER(TRIM(sku)) ----
    orders = orders.reset_index(drop=True)
    orders["_row_id"] = orders.index
    orders["sku_norm"] = orders["sku"].apply(_norm_sku)

    price_list = price_list.copy()
    price_list["_sku_norm_lkp"] = price_list["sku"].apply(_norm_sku)

    # ---- lookup ----
    # NULL sku_norm never matches -> only consider rows with non-null sku_norm
    valid_orders = orders[orders["sku_norm"].notna()]

    if len(valid_orders) > 0 and len(price_list) > 0:
        merged = valid_orders.merge(
            price_list,
            left_on="sku_norm",
            right_on="_sku_norm_lkp",
            suffixes=("", "_pl"),
        )
        # condition: valid_from <= order_date
        merged = merged[merged["valid_from"] <= merged["order_date"]]

        if len(merged) > 0:
            # multiple match tie-break: GREATEST valid_from, then LOWEST list_id
            merged = merged.sort_values(
                ["_row_id", "valid_from", "list_id"],
                ascending=[True, False, True],
                kind="mergesort",
            )
            best = merged.drop_duplicates(subset="_row_id", keep="first")
            best = best[["_row_id", "unit_price"]]
        else:
            best = pd.DataFrame(columns=["_row_id", "unit_price"])
    else:
        best = pd.DataFrame(columns=["_row_id", "unit_price"])

    result = orders.merge(best, on="_row_id", how="left", suffixes=("", "_lkp"))

    result["price_flag"] = np.where(result["unit_price"].notna(), "OK", "NO_PRICE")
    result["unit_price"] = result["unit_price"].fillna(0)

    # ---- expression: ext_amount = qty * unit_price (NULL qty -> NULL ext_amount) ----
    result["ext_amount"] = result["qty"] * result["unit_price"]
    # when qty is NaN, qty * unit_price is NaN automatically via pandas arithmetic

    # ---- router ----
    qty = result["qty"]
    ext_amount = result["ext_amount"]
    price_flag = result["price_flag"]

    mask1 = (price_flag == "NO_PRICE") | qty.isna() | (qty >= 100)
    mask2 = ext_amount >= 1000
    mask3 = ext_amount < 50

    # fillna(False) to make NaN comparisons explicitly False (not true)
    mask1 = mask1.fillna(False)
    mask2 = mask2.fillna(False)
    mask3 = mask3.fillna(False)

    route = np.full(len(result), "STANDARD", dtype=object)
    route = np.where(mask3.to_numpy(), "SMALL", route)
    route = np.where(mask2.to_numpy(), "BULK", route)
    route = np.where(mask1.to_numpy(), "REVIEW", route)

    result["route"] = route

    # ---- output 1: order_enriched ----
    order_enriched = result[["order_id", "sku_norm", "unit_price", "route"]].copy()

    # ---- aggregator: group by route, order_date ----
    grouped = result.groupby(["route", "order_date"], dropna=False)

    order_count = grouped.size().rename("order_count")
    total_ext = grouped["ext_amount"].sum(min_count=0).rename("total_ext")
    # sum with skipna=True by default; all-NaN group yields 0.0 naturally

    agg = pd.concat([order_count, total_ext], axis=1).reset_index()

    route_daily = agg[["route", "order_date", "order_count", "total_ext"]].copy()

    return {
        "order_enriched": order_enriched,
        "route_daily": route_daily,
    }
